title: How Vision AI Verifies Every Step of an SOP
summary: Automate SOP verification with Roboflow: train an action recognition model on your existing cameras to catch missed steps on every unit.
body_markdown:
Summary


**To verify SOPs on every unit instead of in periodic audits, train an action recognition model in Roboflow on clips from your existing station cameras, then compare its step timeline against the written procedure so missed or out-of-order steps get flagged at the station. Add object detection for parts, tools, and PPE, run it on the edge or on-prem, and send deviations to your MES for a per-unit record that supports ISO 9001, IATF 16949, and FDA 21 CFR Part 11.**


A standard operating procedure only protects quality if you can show it was followed on every unit and shift.


Quality[SOP](https://roboflow.com/ai/sop-compliance-monitoring?ref=blog.roboflow.com) implementation requires two separate jobs. SOP authoring gets the procedure written down and taught, while SOP verification confirms each step happened at the station, in order, with the right part, tool, and PPE.


Verifying process compliance typically depends on periodic audits, manual sampling, and on-site checks by supervisors. But often failures show up in reworks, OEE numbers slipping, or customer complaints.


Vision AI closes that gap by checking each step as it's performed, flagging a missed step before the work moves on, and keeping a record of every unit that quality teams and auditors can use.


## Vision AI Confirms Every Step on Every Unit


SOP verification compares work against a written procedure while it's happening, so problems surface at the station instead of in a later audit. For every unit it confirms:


- **Order:** every step in the sequence was followed and completed.
- **Parts and tools:** the right part came from the right bin, and the right tool was used.
- **PPE and safety:** gloves, eye protection, or[cleanroom gowning](https://roboflow.com/ai/aseptic-process-monitoring?ref=blog.roboflow.com) were in place before the step started, and safety steps like guard closure and[lockout](https://roboflow.com/ai/lockout-tagout-verification?ref=blog.roboflow.com) were followed.
- **Timing:** each step ran within its[target time](https://roboflow.com/ai/cycle-time-monitoring?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , without being rushed or running long.


Vision AI enables proactive fast correction, saving time and increasing revenue. We at Roboflow hear that every additional station a unit passes through with an uncaught defect increases the eventual cost by 2x-10x. Operators expect their work environment to support their work, so Roboflow offers on-station[HMIs](https://roboflow.com/blog/hmi-design?ref=blog.roboflow.com) that can be used to provide immediate supportive feedback.


Every unit can also get a record with a clip of each step, giving quality teams and auditors visual evidence of how the work was done in place of a signed checklist.


Vision AI can be used to address workforce skills gaps by lowering the bar to skill qualification and making learning a new on-floor skill easier. New employees can easily follow on-screen work instructions to learn new stations or skills.


## Build an SOP Verification Model in Four Steps


Roboflow recognizes SOP steps with[action recognition](https://roboflow.com/ai/action-recognition?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , a project type built for video. Instead of finding objects in a single frame, an action recognition model watches a clip and returns a timeline of which steps happened and when. A full walkthrough, including training settings, is in our[Cosmos 3 Edge fine-tuning tutorial](https://roboflow.com/blog/fine-tune-cosmos-3-edge?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .


### Step 1: Record clips of the full task


Collect a few dozen short clips from the camera you'll use in production, with the same angle and lighting the model will see on the line. Each clip should show the full procedure from start to finish, and you can add clips and retrain as the model improves.


### Step 2: Label each step on a timeline


Mark where each step starts and ends in Roboflow's video editor by dragging across a timeline, with one row per step and no bounding boxes to draw. Starting each segment at the first movement and ending it when the step finishes teaches the model where one step stops and the next begins.


### Step 3: Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge


Create a dataset version and train Cosmos 3 Edge. At the default settings, the model reads 64 frames at a time, or about 16 seconds of video, which lets it tell apart steps that look alike in a single frame but involve different motion.


### Step 4: Compare the timeline to your SOP


Run new footage through the model and compare its timeline against the procedure to confirm every step is present, in order, and within its target time. Deviations can go to a dashboard, an alert, or your MES.


Action recognition covers the sequence of steps, while object detection checks the details within each one, such as which part, bin, tool, or PPE is in view. For steps that are hard to define with bounding boxes, a vision language model can confirm the state of the station once the step is done.


## Run SOP Verification on your Existing Cameras and Infrastructure


A station is ready for SOP verification as soon as it has a camera with a clear line of sight to the work. Customers can use existing cameras, work with a Roboflow SOP partner, or purchase suitable cameras through Roboflow. Roboflow can use overhead, station, and bench cameras a line already has, so a first deployment rarely requires new hardware.


Models can run on the edge at the line, on-prem, air-gapped, or in a VPC, which keeps video inside the plant when it needs to stay there. Step events and deviations connect to the MES, PLCs, and electronic batch records a plant already uses, and the per-unit record supports the documentation requirements in standards like ISO 9001, IATF 16949, cGMP, and FDA 21 CFR Part 11.


## Set Clear Rules for Operator Video


Ensure your SOP implementation focuses on the work and not the operator. SOP verification exists to catch a skipped step before it becomes a defect and to document that the process held, so the focus stays on process quality and audit records. Any imagery collected should be properly protective of personal information and employee privacy laws.


Each plant decides how deviations are handled and how operator video is used and retained, and Roboflow can run entirely on-prem or air-gapped so footage never leaves the facility. The same step data that flags a miss also shows trainers which steps new operators find hardest, which turns verification into a coaching tool as much as a quality check.


## Bring SOP Verification to Your Line


A procedure on paper is a plan, and a procedure checked on every unit is a process you can prove. That verified, step-by-step record of how the work gets done today also becomes the baseline for longer-term digital twin and factory-of-the-future projects.
